name: Olca Ái

attributes.attribute: a giant who frightened the women of Connacht
leader of the women after whom the lake is named
site of stone sculptures in Lough Erne

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Olca Ái is an Irish hero. This giant once terrified the women of the Connacht capital. They ran from him across the land. Still afraid, they drowned in a great stretch of water. The lake was named for Erne, who led them. Rough stone sculptures at White Island on Lough Erne may show the giant with one of the maidens.

okr.objective: Olca Ái is an Irish giant tied to the naming of Lough Erne.
key_results: Olca Ái is an Irish hero described as a giant.
He frightened the women of the Connacht capital into fleeing.
The lake where they drowned took the name of their leader Erne.
Stone sculptures on White Island may show him with a maiden.
